subtopics.title: Continental Drift and the Evidence for It

questions.question: Wegener proposed that the continents once formed a single supercontinent that began fragmenting about 200 million years ago, called:
options: Pangaea, splitting into Laurasia in the north and Gondwana in the south
Atlantis, splitting into Europe and Africa
Laurasia, splitting into two Pangaeas
Gondwana, splitting into Laurasia and Pangaea

questions.question: Mesosaurus supports continental drift because it was:
options: A strong ocean swimmer found on every continent
A freshwater reptile that could not cross open ocean, yet occurs in the Karoo rocks of South Africa and in beds of identical age in Brazil
A bird that migrated between continents
A plant with wind-blown seeds

questions.question: The Dwyka tillite and the glacial pavements near Barkly West count as CLIMATIC evidence because they show that:
options: South Africa has always been hot and dry
Glaciers still exist in the Karoo today
A continental ice sheet once covered part of what is now a warm country — and the ice-scratch directions only radiate from one centre when the southern continents are reassembled
Coal forms in cold climates

questions.question: Wegener's theory was rejected for decades mainly because:
options: His fossil evidence was proved wrong
The coastlines do not actually fit
He never published his idea
He could not explain the MECHANISM — what force actually moved the continents

subtopics.title: The Engine — Convection Currents and Sea-Floor Spreading

questions.question: A mantle convection current, correctly worded, is:
options: Solid rock deforming plastically — hotter, less dense rock creeps up, spreads sideways, cools, and sinks, at only centimetres per year
A river of liquid lava circling the planet
Ocean water sinking into the mantle
Gas bubbles rising through the crust

questions.question: Slab pull is the force in which:
options: Gravity slides a plate off the raised ridge crest
The sinking edge of a cold, dense plate drags the rest of the plate after it — now regarded as the stronger driver
The moon's gravity tows plates along
Wind pushes the continents

questions.question: The AGE evidence for sea-floor spreading is that ocean-floor rock is:
options: The same age everywhere
Oldest at the ridge and younger toward the continents
Newest at the ridge crest, steadily older outward, and nowhere older than about 200 million years
Older than any continental rock

questions.question: The magnetic stripes on the ocean floor prove spreading because they:
options: All point permanently north
Appear only near the continents
Occur randomly with no pattern
Record the field's reversals in cooling lava and MIRROR each other symmetrically on either side of the ridge

questions.question: Divergent boundaries are also called CONSTRUCTIVE because:
options: New crust is created where magma rises into the gap between separating plates
Buildings survive their earthquakes
They construct trenches
Old crust is destroyed there

questions.question: The East African Rift Valley formed when:
options: Two continents collided head-on
Tension stretched the crust, two parallel fault systems formed, and the strip between them subsided, leaving a flat floor between high fault scarps
A meteorite carved the valley
A single volcano collapsed

questions.question: Which set of features belongs to the East African Rift?
options: The Mariana Trench and island arcs
The San Andreas Fault and offset streams
Deep ribbon lakes such as Tanganyika and Malawi, and volcanoes such as Kilimanjaro along the fractures
The Andes and the Peru-Chile Trench

questions.question: A transform boundary such as the San Andreas Fault has NO volcanoes because:
options: The crust there is too old to melt
Its earthquakes shake magma back down
It lies too far from the sea
Plates slide past each other — nothing descends, so nothing melts

questions.question: Where an oceanic plate meets a continental plate, the oceanic plate subducts because it is:
options: Denser — about 3,0 g/cm³ against the continent's 2,7
Smaller in area
Moving faster
Thicker than the continent

questions.question: The fixed landform kit of an oceanic-continental collision, shown on South America's west coast, is:
options: A rift valley, ribbon lakes and fissure volcanoes
An offshore trench, fold mountains along the margin, and composite volcanoes threaded along those mountains
A mid-ocean ridge and magnetic stripes
Block mountains and a flat plateau

questions.question: When two oceanic plates converge, the result is:
options: The highest fold mountains on earth
A continental rift valley
A trench plus an ISLAND ARC — a curved line of volcanoes such as the Aleutians or Indonesia — with the older, colder, denser plate subducting
No landforms at all

questions.question: Continental-continental collision, as in the Himalayas, produces:
options: Chains of composite volcanoes
A deep ocean trench
An island arc
The loftiest fold mountains and severe earthquakes, but effectively NO volcanoes — no slab descends to make magma

questions.question: In the torn-photograph picture, the matching torn edge stands for:
options: The coastline fit — South America nesting into the curve of West Africa
The magnetic stripes
The convection currents
The Ring of Fire

questions.question: The 'picture running across the tear' — the stronger proof — includes:
options: The depth of the Mariana Trench
Mesosaurus in both the Karoo and Brazil, Glossopteris across five southern lands, and the Cape Fold rocks continuing in Argentina and Antarctica
The speed of P-waves
The height of Kilimanjaro

questions.question: The single missing piece that sank Wegener's theory for fifty years was:
options: He had no fossil examples
The coastlines refused to match
He could not say what force did the pushing
He never visited South Africa

questions.question: In the milk-pot picture, the skin that forms on the warming milk stands for:
options: The lithosphere — the crust plus the rigid top of the mantle, dragged around by the circulation beneath
The liquid outer core
The ocean's surface
The asthenosphere

questions.question: The 'belt half over the edge of a table' explains:
options: Ridge push at the spreading crest
Slab pull — a sinking plate edge whose weight hauls in the rest of the plate
The formation of magnetic stripes
Why the mantle is liquid

questions.question: The sea floor is striped 'like a barcode' because:
options: Different lavas have different colours
Sediment settles in bands
Cooling lava locks in the magnetic direction of its moment, and the field flips now and then — with the west-side barcode mirroring the east
Ships have painted survey lines on it

questions.question: The mantle's convection turns at roughly the speed at which:
options: A car drives on a highway
A river flows
Sound travels through rock
Your hair grows — a few centimetres per year

questions.question: The three moves plates can make, with their proper names, are:
options: Apart (constructive), together (destructive), and past (conservative)
Up, down and sideways
Fast, slow and stopped
Melting, freezing and floating

questions.question: When a sea-floor plate meets a continental plate, the sea floor dives underneath because it is:
options: Thinner and more flexible
The HEAVIER of the two — producing a trench, coastal fold mountains and volcanoes, as on the west of South America
Pushed down by ocean water
Younger than the continent

questions.question: The 'gift fact' about two continents colliding is:
options: It produces the deepest trenches
It creates new oceanic crust
Huge mountains, huge earthquakes and NO volcanoes — nothing sinks, so nothing melts
It happens only under the sea

questions.question: The giveaway landform of the scraping-past move is:
options: A curved chain of volcanic islands
A wide flat rift floor with ribbon lakes
A ring of composite volcanoes
A long dead-straight fault scar with streams, roads and fences stepped sideways across it
